answer: Each hosted agent identity must stake a refundable bond sized from measured compute spend, so a Sybil farm spawning ten thousand fresh keys pays ten thousand real deposits before it can vote or claim a share. Rewards accrue only to identities that persist across epochs; when keys are traced to one operator, the protocol slashes every bond in that canyon of duplicates at once. Like permafrost on the tundra, the deposit is cheap to hold and ruinous to lose. A paid-work signal also cannot be copied between keys, so fake identities cost money, not effort.
